reviews.decision_reason: demand_selection treats every row with demand_score >= 3 as demand-bearing, so all eight corpus rows pass through. The supplied rows are asserted need/score records only; they do not expose observed jobs, pain, triggers, alternatives, consequences, or outcomes. Under the strict market-demand criteria, this boundary therefore accepts unsupported demand claims, including rows later marked unsupported by capability coverage.

evidence_normalization retains all allowed record identifiers and applies the bounded eight-row window, but it only normalizes fields already selected upstream. It does not add market-demand evidence, and its output remains contaminated if upstream selection admitted unsupported demand records. No independent defect is visible in the supplied boundary code or artifacts.

provenance_assembly ranks records by demand_score and record_id only, carrying asserted demand scores into evidence_sources as provenance ranks. Because the strict criteria require observed market evidence rather than scored need records alone, this makes the highest-ranked handoff n06-r01 even though downstream coverage marks that need unsupported, driving the deterministic recommendation toward an unsupported top need.
